EHRTemplate.Description: Structured protocol for safely tapering and discontinuing antidepressant medication. Includes withdrawal symptom monitoring, relapse detection, and evidence-based tapering schedules.

EvidenceBase.Guideline: NICE CG90 Depression - Continue 6-12 months after remission
NICE CG90 - Taper over 4+ weeks to reduce withdrawal

Section.Title: Eligibility for Deprescribing
Section.Description: Determine if patient is appropriate candidate for stopping antidepressant

Field.Label: Current PHQ-9 Score
Field.Link: Link to most recent PHQ-9 assessment
Field.Alert: PHQ-9 ≥ 5 indicates not in remission - stopping medication NOT recommended

Field.Label: Duration of Remission (months)
Field.Guidance: Remission defined as PHQ-9 < 5. How many months has patient maintained remission?
Field.Alert: Less than 6 months remission - NICE recommends continuing treatment. Consider waiting.

Field.Label: Depression History
Field.Guidance: - First episode: Can consider stopping after 6-12 months remission - Second episode: Consider stopping after 12-24 months remission - Recurrent (3+): Consider long-term/indefinite treatment

Field.Label: Previous Relapse When Stopped Medication?

Options.Option: No - never stopped before OR stopped successfully

Field.Alert: Previous relapse on stopping indicates high risk - consider long-term treatment or very slow taper with close monitoring

Field.Label: Current Life Stressors Present?
Field.Guidance: Avoid stopping during periods of high stress (relationship breakdown, bereavement, job loss, major life changes)
Field.Alert: Current life stressors present - consider delaying deprescribing until situation stabilizes

Field.Label: Lifestyle Interventions Maintained?

Options.Option: Yes - exercising regularly, good sleep, social connection maintained
No - not maintaining protective lifestyle factors

Field.Guidance: Lifestyle interventions (especially exercise) reduce relapse risk. Strongly encourage maintaining before stopping medication.
Field.Alert: Lifestyle interventions not maintained - strongly recommend establishing exercise/sleep/social routine before stopping medication to reduce relapse risk

Field.Label: Patient Preference Regarding Stopping

Options.Option: Patient ambivalent (both wants to stop and fears relapse)

Field.Guidance: Shared decision-making: Patient preference important. Discuss pros/cons.

Options.Option: Eligible - Low risk (first episode, 6-12+ months remission, stable, lifestyle maintained)
Eligible - Moderate risk (some risk factors present, will need close monitoring)
Eligible - High risk (multiple risk factors, very slow taper essential, close monitoring)
NOT eligible - Recurrent depression, recommend long-term treatment
DEFER - Current stressors, recommend revisit in 3-6 months

Field.Label: Rationale for Eligibility Decision
Field.Placeholder: Clinical reasoning: Why is patient eligible/not eligible? What risk factors considered?

Section.Title: Shared Decision-Making: Stopping Antidepressant
Section.Description: Discuss risks, benefits, and alternatives with patient

Options.Option: No more side effects (sexual, weight, emotional blunting)
Psychological benefit of managing without medication
Avoid long-term medication if not needed
Relapse risk (50% after stopping vs 20-30% if continuing for 1+ years)
Withdrawal symptoms (dizziness, flu-like, electric shocks, anxiety, insomnia)
Withdrawal can last weeks to months if not tapered slowly
Difficulty distinguishing withdrawal from relapse initially
May need to restart medication if relapse occurs
Continue medication indefinitely (especially if recurrent depression)
Reduce to lower dose (rather than stopping completely)
Wait longer (more time in remission reduces relapse risk)
Switch to therapy (e.g., MBCT for relapse prevention)

Field.Label: Patient Understanding Confirmed?

Options.Option: Yes - patient understands risks, withdrawal symptoms, and need for slow taper

Field.Guidance: Ensure patient has realistic expectations about withdrawal and relapse risk

Section.Title: Tapering Protocol
Section.Description: Evidence-based tapering schedule based on medication and individual factors

Field.Label: Medication Half-Life Category

Options.Option: Long half-life (fluoxetine 4-6 days) - slower taper less critical
Medium half-life (sertraline, citalopram, escitalopram ~1 day) - standard taper
Short half-life (paroxetine, venlafaxine ~12 hours) - very slow taper essential

Field.Guidance: - Long (fluoxetine): Self-tapering due to long half-life, withdrawal less severe - Medium (sertraline, citalopram, escitalopram): Taper over 4-8+ weeks - Short (paroxetine, venlafaxine): Taper over 8-12+ weeks minimum, very high withdrawal risk

Field.Label: Duration on Medication
Field.Guidance: Longer duration on medication requires slower taper

Field.Label: Current Dose Compared to Starting Dose
Field.Guidance: If on higher dose, may need to reduce to starting dose first, then taper further

Field.Label: Tapering Speed Recommended

Options.Option: Very slow (12-24+ weeks) - High risk: short half-life, long duration on med, previous withdrawal issues, patient anxious
Slow (8-12 weeks) - Standard for most medications
Moderate (4-6 weeks) - Long half-life (fluoxetine), low risk

Field.AutoPopulate: Based on half-life, duration, and risk factors
Field.Alert: Short half-life medication (paroxetine, venlafaxine) should use very slow taper - moderate taper will cause severe withdrawal

Field.Label: Specific Tapering Schedule
Field.Placeholder: Document exact tapering schedule, e.g.: - Weeks 1-2: 100mg daily (current dose) - Weeks 3-4: 75mg daily (25% reduction) - Weeks 5-6: 50mg daily - Weeks 7-8: 25mg daily - Weeks 9-10: 25mg every other day - Week 11+: Stop Monitor at each step, can slow down if withdrawal symptoms
Field.Guidance: General principle: Reduce by 25% every 2-4 weeks, slower as get to lower doses

Options.Option: Dose reduction (reduce dose at constant frequency)

Field.Label: Patient Understands Tapering Can Be Slowed?

Options.Option: Yes - patient knows can slow down or pause if withdrawal symptoms

Field.Guidance: Emphasize: Not a race. If withdrawal symptoms occur, slow down or pause. Individualized approach.

Options.Option: Common withdrawal symptoms explained (dizziness, electric shocks, flu-like, anxiety, insomnia, vivid dreams)
Timeline explained (start 2-7 days after dose reduction, peak 1-2 weeks, usually resolve 2-6 weeks)
How to distinguish withdrawal from relapse
Management strategies (slow taper, symptomatic relief, reassurance)
When to contact doctor (severe symptoms, persistent symptoms, concern about relapse)

Field.Label: Relapse Prevention Strategies Discussed

Options.Option: Maintain exercise (150 min/week) throughout taper and after
Consider therapy booster sessions during taper
Consider MBCT (Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy) for relapse prevention
Patient knows early warning signs of relapse

Field.Guidance: Lifestyle interventions crucial during taper - reduce relapse risk

Field.Label: Expected Complete Stop Date (if taper goes as planned)
Field.Guidance: May extend if withdrawal symptoms require slower taper

Section.Title: Monitoring During Tapering
Section.Description: To be completed at each monitoring visit during taper

Field.Label: Current Taper Stage
Field.Placeholder: e.g., "Week 5 of taper, currently on 50mg daily (reduced from 100mg)"

Field.Label: Current PHQ-9 Score
Field.Alert: PHQ-9 ≥ 5 - may indicate relapse. Distinguish from withdrawal.
PHQ-9 ≥ 10 - likely relapse. Consider resuming previous dose.

Options.Option: Mild (noticeable but tolerable, not affecting function)

Field.Label: Clinical Assessment: Withdrawal vs. Relapse

Options.Option: Withdrawal symptoms (physical symptoms prominent, started within days of dose reduction, PHQ-9 still low)
Relapse (core depression symptoms return, PHQ-9 ≥ 10, occurred weeks after dose reduction)

Field.Guidance: Withdrawal: Physical symptoms (dizziness, zaps, flu-like), start 2-7 days after reduction, transient Relapse: Psychological symptoms (low mood, anhedonia, hopelessness), gradual onset, persistent

Options.Option: Pause taper (severe withdrawal symptoms - hold at current dose until symptoms resolve)
Increase dose back up one step (intolerable withdrawal)

Field.Label: Taper Adjustment Details (if adjustment needed)
Field.Placeholder: Specific adjustment made and rationale, e.g., "Severe dizziness and electric shocks on reducing to 50mg. Increased back to 75mg, will hold for 4 weeks then try smaller reduction (to 62.5mg using liquid formulation)."

Options.Option: Symptomatic treatment (antihistamines for dizziness, analgesics for headache)
Slower taper or smaller dose reductions
Switch to liquid formulation for finer adjustments
Temporarily increase dose slightly then resume slower taper

Field.Label: Patient Maintaining Relapse Prevention Strategies?

Options.Option: Yes - exercising, sleep good, social connections maintained

Field.Alert: Lifestyle interventions lapsed - strongly encourage reestablishing (reduces relapse risk significantly)

Field.Label: Next Monitoring Visit
Field.Guidance: Monitor closely during taper: every 2-4 weeks, more frequently if withdrawal symptoms or relapse concern

Section.Title: Post-Discontinuation Monitoring
Section.Description: Monitoring after medication completely stopped - detect relapse early

Field.Label: Current PHQ-9 Score
Field.Alert: PHQ-9 ≥ 10 - relapse occurring, consider restarting treatment

Options.Option: Subsyndromal symptoms (PHQ-9 5-9, not full relapse yet)
New life stressor (bereavement, job loss, relationship, etc.)
Watchful waiting with close monitoring (if subsyndromal only)
Same medication previously on (known to work)

Field.Label: Restart Dose
Field.Placeholder: Usually restart at previously effective dose

Field.Label: Long-Term Treatment Plan After Relapse

Options.Option: Continue for longer duration (e.g., 2 years) then reassess stopping

Field.Guidance: Relapse after stopping indicates patient may need long-term treatment

Field.Label: Duration of Persistent Withdrawal (weeks since stopped)

Options.Option: Reassurance - most withdrawal resolves eventually (can take 3-6 months)
Consider restarting medication and tapering much more slowly

Field.Label: Lifestyle Interventions Maintained Post-Stop?

Options.Option: Yes - exercise, sleep, social connections maintained

Field.Alert: Lifestyle not maintained - high relapse risk, strongly encourage reestablishing

Field.Label: Post-Discontinuation Monitoring Frequency
Field.Guidance: Highest relapse risk in first 6 months after stopping - monitor closely

Options.Option: Side effects acceptable, medication working well
Current life stressors, not good time to stop

Field.Label: Monitoring Plan While Continuing
Field.DefaultValue: PHQ-9 every 6-12 months to ensure maintaining remission. Annual discussion about whether to continue or stop.

Rule.Alert: Patient not in remission (PHQ-9 ≥ 5). Stopping medication NOT recommended per NICE guideline. Continue treatment until achieve and maintain remission for 6-12 months.
Remission < 6 months. NICE recommends continuing treatment for 6-12 months after remission to prevent relapse. Consider waiting.
Recurrent depression (3+ episodes). Consider long-term/indefinite treatment. If stopping attempted, very slow taper and close monitoring essential.
Patient relapsed when stopped medication previously. High risk of relapse again. Consider long-term treatment or very slow taper (> 6 months) with close monitoring.
Short half-life medication (paroxetine, venlafaxine) with rapid taper. HIGH RISK of severe withdrawal. Use very slow taper (8-24+ weeks) with small dose reductions.
Severe withdrawal symptoms. SLOW DOWN or PAUSE taper. May need to increase dose back up one step, then taper more slowly. Consider liquid formulation for finer dose adjustments.
Relapse during taper (PHQ-9 ≥ 10). Consider resuming previous effective dose. Patient may need long-term treatment.
Relapse after stopping medication. Restart treatment. Consider long-term/indefinite treatment given relapse on stopping.
Lifestyle interventions not maintained post-stopping. High relapse risk. Strongly encourage reestablishing exercise (150 min/week), good sleep, social connections.
Current significant life stressors present. Consider deferring deprescribing until situation stabilizes (reduces relapse risk).

Medication.name: Sertraline
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - Starting dose usually 50mg - If on higher dose (100-200mg), reduce to 50mg over 4-8 weeks first - From 50mg: Reduce to 25mg for 2-4 weeks - Then 25mg alternate days for 2 weeks - Then stop - Total taper time: 8-12 weeks minimum
Medication.Notes: Available as 50mg and 100mg tablets. 25mg not standard - may need to split 50mg tablets or use liquid formulation (50mg/ml solution).

Medication.name: Fluoxetine
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - Long half-life means "self-tapering" - Can often stop without gradual taper (discuss with patient) - If prefer taper: Reduce to 20mg for 2 weeks, then stop - Or alternate day dosing for 1-2 weeks then stop - Total taper time: 2-4 weeks often sufficient
Medication.Notes: Withdrawal symptoms less severe and less common than other SSRIs due to long half-life. Preferred SSRI if patient has concerns about withdrawal.

Medication.name: Citalopram
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - Standard dose 20mg - Reduce to 10mg for 2-4 weeks - Then 10mg alternate days for 2 weeks - Then stop - Total taper time: 6-8 weeks
Medication.Notes: Available as 10mg, 20mg, 40mg tablets. Also liquid formulation (40mg/ml drops) for fine dose adjustments.

Medication.name: Escitalopram
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - Standard dose 10mg - Reduce to 5mg for 2-4 weeks - Then 5mg alternate days for 2 weeks - Then stop - Total taper time: 6-8 weeks
Medication.Notes: Available as 5mg, 10mg, 20mg tablets. Also liquid formulation for fine adjustments.

Medication.name: Paroxetine
Medication.HalfLife: 21 hours (but potent anticholinergic effects cause severe withdrawal)
Medication.WithdrawalRisk: VERY HIGH - worst SSRI for withdrawal
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - MUST taper very slowly - From 20mg: Reduce to 15mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 10mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 5mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 2.5mg (half of 5mg) for 2-3 weeks - Then 2.5mg alternate days for 2 weeks - Then stop - Total taper time: 12-20+ weeks minimum - Consider liquid formulation (10mg/5ml suspension) for very gradual reductions
Medication.Notes: Paroxetine causes most severe and common withdrawal symptoms of any SSRI. Very slow taper essential. If severe withdrawal on tapering, consider switching to fluoxetine first (cross-taper), then stop fluoxetine (easier withdrawal).
Medication.Warning: DO NOT stop abruptly - severe withdrawal almost guaranteed

Medication.name: Venlafaxine
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - MUST taper very slowly - Example from 150mg: - Reduce to 112.5mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 75mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 37.5mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 18.75mg (use liquid or tablet splitting) for 2-3 weeks - Then alternate day dosing for 2 weeks - Then stop - Total taper time: 12-20+ weeks minimum - Consider dose reductions of no more than 25mg every 3-4 weeks
Medication.Notes: Venlafaxine has very high withdrawal rate - 60-70% experience withdrawal symptoms. Available as 37.5mg, 75mg, 150mg XL. May need to split tablets or compound liquid for intermediate doses. Monitor blood pressure during taper (venlafaxine can raise BP - may drop when stopping).
Medication.Warning: Severe withdrawal common - "brain zaps", dizziness, nausea. Very slow taper essential.

Medication.name: Duloxetine
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - From 60mg: Reduce to 30mg for 3-4 weeks - Then 20mg for 2-3 weeks (may need to open capsule and remove beads - discuss with pharmacist) - Then alternate day dosing - Then stop - Total taper time: 8-12 weeks
Medication.Notes: Available as 30mg and 60mg capsules (delayed-release). Intermediate doses challenging - may need to count beads inside capsule or work with compounding pharmacist.

Medication.name: Mirtazapine
Medication.TaperingProtocol: - From 30mg: Reduce to 15mg for 2-4 weeks - Then 7.5mg (half tablet) for 2-3 weeks - Then 7.5mg alternate days for 1-2 weeks - Then stop - Total taper time: 6-10 weeks
Medication.Notes: Available as 15mg, 30mg, 45mg tablets (also orodispersible). Sedating effect may reduce during taper - warn patient sleep may be affected. Insomnia common withdrawal symptom.

Metric.Label: Appropriate Duration Before Stopping Attempted
Metric.Calculation: Percentage with ≥ 6 months remission before deprescribing

Metric.Label: Successful Discontinuation Rate (12 months)
Metric.Calculation: Percentage remaining off medication 12 months after discontinuation without relapse

Metric.Label: Relapse Rate After Stopping
Metric.Calculation: Percentage experiencing relapse (PHQ-9 ≥ 10) within 12 months of stopping

Metric.Label: Medication Restart Rate
Metric.Calculation: Percentage restarting medication within 12 months of stopping

System.name: EMIS
System.Instructions: 1. Create deprescribing template 2. Link to treatment plan and monitoring templates 3. Set up alerts for high-risk medications (paroxetine, venlafaxine) 4. Automated tapering schedule generation 5. Reminders for monitoring visits during taper 6. Flag in patient record "TAPERING ANTIDEPRESSANT" for continuity

System.name: SystmOne
System.Instructions: 1. Deprescribing template in care plan 2. Link to repeat prescription for dose adjustments 3. Automated tasks for monitoring during taper 4. Post-discontinuation follow-up reminders

System.name: Vision
System.Instructions: 1. Custom deprescribing form 2. Integration with prescription module for dose changes 3. Diary reminders for monitoring

UsageNotes.Note: Use this template when considering stopping antidepressant medication after achieving remission.
Not all patients should stop - recurrent depression (3+ episodes) may warrant long-term treatment.
Shared decision-making essential - patient preference and risk/benefit discussion.
Slow tapering (≥ 4 weeks, ideally 8-12+ weeks) reduces withdrawal symptoms.
Short half-life medications (paroxetine, venlafaxine) require very slow taper (12-20+ weeks).
Monitor closely during taper - distinguish withdrawal from relapse.
Withdrawal symptoms usually resolve 2-6 weeks after each dose reduction.
If relapse occurs during/after taper, consider long-term treatment.
Maintain lifestyle interventions (exercise, sleep, social) throughout taper and after - reduces relapse risk.
Highest relapse risk in first 6 months after stopping - monitor closely.
